entries.title: Decoder latency is not universally tens of microseconds
entries.next_action: Make a versioned hardware timing table with explicit pulse, syndrome, decoder and feedback endpoints.
alternatives: Original surface-code projection retained as a separate scenario
acceptance: Every latency has a primary-source locator, date, code distance, logical error and demonstrated/projected label.
No small-code result replaces an application-scale clock without an H18 failure check.
entries.stop_rule: Screen the existing anchors plus at most two newer primary constructions; missing sustained-error data closes that substitution.
entries.on_pass: Pass admissible timing records to H03/H17; retain old scenarios with their dates.
entries.on_fail: Mark unsupported replacements unavailable and continue with the bounded scenarios.
steps: Recover each timing boundary from its figure/table.
Separate single-shot delay from sustained throughput.
Apply H18's whole-computation admissibility test.

entries.title: Fast standalone decoding is not the entire reaction loop
entries.next_action: Build one end-to-end reaction-loop timeline from acquisition through transport, decoding and conditional pulse dispatch.
acceptance: All serial stages are charged; overlap has a stated dependency reason.
Kernel latency and complete reaction latency are distinct fields.
entries.stop_rule: Stop after two complete timelines; an unmeasured link remains an explicit parameter, not zero.
entries.on_pass: Feed the measured/projected loop into H03.
entries.on_fail: Retain a sensitivity interval; reject a claimed nanosecond layer based only on a kernel.
steps: Identify link bandwidth and synchronization requirements.
Check whether feedback waits for one syndrome or many.
Export bottleneck and endpoints.

entries.title: A code cycle and a logical T layer are different quantities
entries.next_action: Map a short signed multiply-add chain into reaction dependencies, independent of the code-cycle duration.
alternatives: Time-optimal teleportation with explicit prepared resources
acceptance: Every measurement that gates a later operation is represented.
Count preparation, feedforward, connectivity and extra workspace; recover the original schedule as a control.
entries.stop_rule: Compare two gate schedules for one leaf and one dependent chain; no whole-source credit before a compatible mapping exists.
entries.on_pass: Scale the accepted mapping in H17 and check factory demand in H05/H06.
entries.on_fail: Keep the conventional mapping and record the failed assumptions.
steps: Choose a leaf already emitted in the latest library.
Construct a dependency timeline under each schedule.
Compare latency and qubits at equal failure allowance.

entries.title: Repeating distance-many syndrome rounds per operation is not mandatory in every architecture
entries.next_action: Make an assumption-to-circuit checklist for a transversal fault-tolerance construction using one existing adder.
acceptance: Transversal gate set, input magic-state quality, decoder, connectivity and accumulated failures satisfy the construction.
Finite resources are recorded; constant rounds are not equated to a fixed nanosecond clock.
entries.stop_rule: One finite adder mapping and one assumption audit; if a required decoder/gate is absent, defer scaling.
entries.on_pass: Send the compatible gate schedule to H17.
entries.on_fail: Close this direct transfer and retain the missing-interface list.
steps: Identify gates unavailable transversally.
Charge their replacements.
Check whole-run failure and reaction dependencies.

entries.title: Fifteen-to-one distillation is not the only magic-state supply
entries.next_action: Replace only the factory model for the actual T-state demand, keeping the computation and error allowance fixed.
acceptance: Record successful output rate, rejected attempts, footprint, transport and error per output.
Factories, data and routing fit simultaneously; both schemes obey the same total failure allowance.
entries.stop_rule: Compare two factories on one demand profile; absent finite noise/output data makes the cultivation result conditional.
entries.on_pass: Integrate the winning compatible supply into H17.
entries.on_fail: Retain baseline supply and disclose which factory parameters are missing.
steps: Extract time-dependent magic-state demand from the circuit.
Size factories for peak/buffered demand.
Check rate, footprint and failures jointly.

entries.title: T-state supply and Toffoli-state supply must be matched to the circuit
entries.next_action: Export separate CCX, T-rotation and Clifford demands before pricing native Toffoli supply.
alternatives: Native CCZ/Toffoli factory or compatible catalysis
acceptance: One arithmetic CCX is charged exactly once; residual rotations still pay their synthesis demand.
Native gate timing, workspace, state error and routing use one architecture.
entries.stop_rule: Two lowerings for one leaf and one source; reject combinations that remove the same gate twice.
entries.on_pass: Update H05/H17 with the matched state types.
entries.on_fail: Keep seven-T costs as the accepted baseline; native counts remain sensitivity data.
steps: Reconcile with existing native-CCX capacity sensitivity.
Lower the chosen leaf in both gate sets.
Recompute full scheduled demand rather than multiply claimed savings.

entries.title: Distillation is not logically necessary for every non-Clifford implementation
entries.next_action: Translate one adder into a protected cat-qubit gate set and audit its noise assumptions.
acceptance: Bias, leakage, nonadiabatic errors and physical gate durations are stated.
The translated adder implements the same signed modular function and meets the allocated error.
entries.stop_rule: One gate translation; if usable finite error/duration data are missing, stop before full-source extrapolation.
entries.on_pass: Continue with the complete cat architecture in H08.
entries.on_fail: Leave a conditional architectural branch, not a demonstrated timing improvement.
steps: Check gate identities locally on small registers.
Price every correction and protected operation.
Test the noise/error assumption ledger.

entries.title: An alternative physical qubit does not automatically eliminate all factories
entries.next_action: Insert the pricing leaf schedule into a complete cat architecture cost model.
acceptance: Include Toffoli preparation, teleportation, transport and idling.
Use pricing's operation counts and failure budget, not a cryptographic workload's speedup.
entries.stop_rule: One full leaf model; no source claim if gate costs cannot be composed at the actual connectivity.
entries.on_pass: Add an independently labelled hardware scenario to H17.
entries.on_fail: Record the unavailable finite mapping and continue with supported architectures.
steps: Extract finite cost formulas from primary architecture evidence.
Map the same adder/multiplier chain.
Compare simultaneous space and latency.

entries.title: Surface-code physical-qubit overhead is not universal
entries.next_action: Split the source allocation into stored data, active logic, ancillas and factories before substituting qLDPC storage.
alternatives: Bivariate-bicycle/qLDPC storage plus explicit active-gate interfaces
acceptance: Finite code blocks, connectivity, conversion costs and logical error are recorded.
Storage savings exclude active arithmetic and factories unless those mappings are also supplied.
entries.stop_rule: One finite allocation at each current B4/B8 cap; missing memory-to-logic conversion closes this direct integration.
entries.on_pass: Hand the addressable operation interface to H10/H17.
entries.on_fail: Retain memory-only savings as a separate component result.
steps: Measure live storage after A18.
Choose finite code blocks.
Charge all movement between storage and active logic.

entries.title: High-rate codes also have logical-operation research
entries.next_action: Map a 32-bit adder through one finite qLDPC logical-operation scheme.
alternatives: qLDPC Clifford operations plus explicit T mechanism
acceptance: Charge inter-block gates, addressability, measurements and code conversion.
Count finite qubits and operation latency at the required failure rate.
entries.stop_rule: One adder mapping; no full-source projection without a non-Clifford interface.
entries.on_pass: Compare with H03/H17 using the same adder function.
entries.on_fail: Document the missing logic interface and stop this architecture transfer.
steps: Locate the scheme's gate primitives.
Lower each adder gate.
Include nonlocal operation and state-supply costs.

entries.title: Addressable transversal non-Clifford gates are a distinct route
source_sections: 5 root cause B cheap non-Clifford gates
entries.next_action: Find finite parameters for an addressable transversal-CCZ code and map one Toffoli-heavy leaf.
acceptance: Finite block size, stabilizer extraction and physical CCZ connectivity are available.
The construction is not mislabeled LDPC; unused block qubits still count.
entries.stop_rule: One finite parameter extraction; missing physical CCZ/error implementation makes the timing branch unavailable.
entries.on_pass: Compare its compatible state demand and latency with H06.
entries.on_fail: Keep the coding-theory result separate from application cost.
steps: Expand theorem parameters.
Identify an admissible physical gate model.
Count extraction, idle and gate errors.

entries.title: Constant asymptotic overhead is not a small finite constant
entries.next_action: Evaluate the additive-space and width conditions of a constant-overhead construction for the current source width/depth.
acceptance: Compute n, F(n) and required width with the construction's constants.
Missing constants remain unknown; asymptotic O(1) is never assigned an arbitrary numerical overhead.
entries.stop_rule: One full-text finite-constant audit; if no usable construction/constants are supplied, close the numerical-transfer branch.
entries.on_pass: Add a finite admissible scenario to H17 only if all conditions pass.
entries.on_fail: Record a theoretical alternative with no credited crossover.
steps: Insert actual width, depth and total fault probability.
Check the width inequality.
Expand finite code/noise costs or record their absence.

entries.title: Idle space can dominate a physical mapping
entries.next_action: Lower one multiplier to active-volume blocks and compare idle storage and reaction depth at fixed resources.
acceptance: Record memory, active volume, reaction depth and required nonlocal connections.
All three bottlenecks are costed; lower active volume alone is not a latency gain.
entries.stop_rule: One leaf plus one dependent chain; reject any unimplemented connectivity assumption for accepted timing.
entries.on_pass: Extend a compatible mapping through H17.
entries.on_fail: Retain component volume results with explicit missing routing.
steps: Translate primitive gates to blocks.
Count memory dwell and reaction dependencies.
Compare under simultaneous data/factory capacity.

entries.title: Photonic clock rates cannot be inserted directly as logical-layer rates
entries.next_action: Model photonic throughput and feedback delay independently for the same dependency chain.
acceptance: Emitter count, loss, buffer/delay length and decoder throughput are fixed.
Optical clock rate is distinct from dependency latency; losses consume the total fault budget.
entries.stop_rule: One finite resource-generator/delay scenario and one sensitivity interval; missing loss data defers transfer.
entries.on_pass: Insert compatible throughput and reaction limits into H17.
entries.on_fail: Keep the architecture as a conditional route, with no GHz logical-layer substitution.
steps: Determine resource-state consumption.
Size optical buffers and generators.
Calculate latency, loss and sustained output together.

entries.title: Millions of logical qubits in the emitted oracle are not an information lower bound
entries.next_action: Combine the exact compact SSA allocator with the accepted carry-save and ln(2) library and rebuild capped schedules; A18 is needed only for the later recomputation branch.
alternatives: Reversible checkpointing when packing is insufficient
acceptance: Use the unchanged financial target and arbitrary output XOR; restore every input/workspace bit.
Show depth/qubit Pareto results with actual recomputation, not a width estimate alone.
entries.stop_rule: First run packing alone; then at most three checkpoint policies on one segment. Reject any claimed memory gain without a clean replay.
entries.on_pass: Adopt compatible Pareto improvements via C13; expose affordable estimator lanes to E20.
entries.on_fail: Keep the accepted baseline and record the measured width/depth tradeoff.
steps: Reuse the existing exact compact-storage implementation.
Integrate the latest leaf scratch sizes.
Replay B4 and B8 before considering recomputation.

entries.title: Classical parallelism is inexpensive in this benchmark but not literally free
entries.next_action: Measure classical scaling at 1, 2, 4, 8 and up to 16 available workers with identical contracts and seeds.
alternatives: GPU only if already locally available and eligible
acceptance: Report setup, cold one-price time, warm repeated time and throughput separately.
No linear scaling extrapolation beyond measured worker counts; tuning is charged consistently.
entries.stop_rule: One fixed scaling grid; an unavailable GPU arm is marked unavailable rather than triggering a download/cloud job.
entries.on_pass: Use measured scaling in G4 and E20 comparisons.
entries.on_fail: Report saturation/overhead honestly and retain the fastest eligible observed method.
steps: Freeze worker affinity and workload.
Record resource and machine information.
Repeat the prescribed timings with reference-price checks.

entries.title: T depth alone does not determine runtime
entries.next_action: Create one resource ledger for the latest accepted source before attaching any estimator or hardware clock.
alternatives: Explicit compatible schedule for an achievable upper bound
acceptance: Reconcile CCX/T count, T-depth, total logical depth, scratch, memory and data movement.
Label max(reaction,supply,routing,other) a lower bound, not an executable runtime.
Keep B4/B8 knock-out and C4/H8 residual source families separate.
entries.stop_rule: One ledger per source and at most three compatible architectures; missing routing produces an incomplete scenario.
entries.on_pass: Combine G3, G4 and H18 into G5 using actually scheduled overlap.
entries.on_fail: Keep source-only L4 results and mark missing physical interfaces explicitly.
steps: Hash the accepted libraries and schedules.
Extract demand by schedule batch.
Attach architecture inputs only with provenance and matching gate set.

entries.title: Error per operation must fall as the entire computation grows
entries.next_action: Compute required per-operation and per-magic-state failure from the entire estimator invocation schedule.
alternatives: A dependence-aware bound only with a justified theorem
acceptance: Allocate hardware failure within the total 0.01 and count every repeated source, reflection and state use.
Choose code distance and state error jointly with latency and footprint.
entries.stop_rule: Use a provisional count range until G3; reject any fast hardware row whose accumulated failure exceeds its allocation.
entries.on_pass: Recompute H01-H14 admissibility and close G5 only for the complete compatible configuration.
entries.on_fail: Increase protection/reprice, or reject the hardware scenario without changing the financial confidence requirement.
steps: Start from delta/N per opportunity.
Partition code, state and control errors.
Replace provisional counts with the final estimator schedule.
